name: Open blue carbon registry
summary: An open, public registry of blue carbon ecosystems (mangroves, seagrass meadows and salt marshes): where they are, who keeps them, what is measured there, and what has been promised and paid. Every claim carries its sources and settles only when independent lines of evidence agree. It records; it does not issue or sell credits.
input_wanted: Open maps and datasets for mangrove, seagrass and salt-marsh extent
Measurement methods for carbon stocks and their uncertainty
Pilot sites with communities ready to keep and record them
Existing registries to link to rather than duplicate

name: Ocean Data Initiative
summary: Open ocean data, refreshed every week: tide gauges, buoys and Argo floats checked against ocean models, coral reef heat stress, and marine protection and ocean finance for every Atlantic Rim country, as map layers any GIS tool can read.
input_wanted: New open sources and partner datasets
Corrections where a measurement and a model disagree

name: The commons registry
summary: A registry of commons, each placed on the rules ladder (no rules, weak rules, no payout) with its boundaries, users, rules and remuneration, and every claim backed by evidence from independent sources.
input_wanted: Commons to add, with the people who use them
Better evidence for, or against, a claim already listed

name: Library of the Commons
summary: A map of Elinor Ostrom's academic lineage, starting with the 149 Workshop PhDs and affiliated scholars, as the start of a brain trust that can answer place-specific questions about governing a commons.
input_wanted: Scholars missing from the first generation
Later affiliations, current work and key publications
The second generation: students of these scholars

name: Marine protected area pilot
summary: One marine protected area, governed with the people who fish and dive there: clear boundaries, local rules, monitoring that pairs community testimony with independent measurement, and payouts to its keepers.
input_wanted: A candidate MPA with an active local group
Monitoring data and partners on the ground

name: Medicine from biodiversity
summary: Turning the voluntary global benefit-sharing rule for genetic sequence data into payouts that reach the places and peoples the data comes from.
input_wanted: Cases of medicines traced to a specific place or people
Companies willing to contribute and report

name: AI agent commons
summary: Rules for the shared networks where AI agents meet: identity, an accountable owner, a charter they accept, verification that counts agents of one model as one voice, and a levy that funds the commons.
input_wanted: Agent builders willing to join under a charter
Views on fees, findings and appeals for agents
